transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Elliot (Redwood SE), Lena (Cerulean Head of Product), Mateo (CTO), Priya (Eng Manager), Samir (SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to map Cerulean's real-time support routing use case, constraints, and to outline an onramp plan using Redwood's hosted API with evaluation of Dedicated/Private for pilot.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan at redwood, quick sound check?
[00:08] Lena: good here, yep, loud and clear
[00:11] Mateo: all good
[00:15] Jordan: awesome, we'll keep this to discovery. goal is understand your latency/cost needs, timeline, and then propose a quick onramp — free credits, console access, time-to-first-token path. maya will jump in on technicals.
[00:30] Maya: hi all, quick intro — i'm maya, se on the infra team. we usually help run mini-benchmarks and set up a pilot on hosted, then if teams need we talk dedicated or private.
[00:45] Priya: thanks. high level — we run a customer support routing layer, synchronous web requests, 80% of requests need <120ms p95 for routing decisions. we also need storing of transcripts for audit for 1 year and some EU residency.
[01:05] Elliot: got it, so you're doing classification/reranking or generation?
[01:10] Priya: mostly classification + light ranking, occasional short generation for templated replies.
[01:18] Jordan: perfect. sounds like model footprint is modest but latency tight. curious — what's your current stack?
[01:25] Mateo: currently prototype on our infra, we use a mix of open-source models on a cluster, but ops cost and spiky infra are hurting. we want a predictable unit cost and a straightforward dev onramp for product teams.
[01:40] Lena: and time to first token is important — we want interns or PMs to be able to hit the API same day with a cURL or SDK.
[01:48] Maya: that's our sweet spot — hosted API gives fastest TTFT. we give free credits for an eval, SDKs in node/python, sample apps, and a quickstart that gets a dev to first token in under an hour typically.
[02:05] Samir: security questions: do you support SAML SSO, SCIM, KMS integration, and do you provide audit logs we can keep in our SIEM?
[02:16] Jordan: yes on SAML/SCIM and audit logs. For keys we integrate with customer KMS in Private deployments; Hosted can use CMKs for enterprise tiers. we'll share the security pack.
[02:30] Maya: also, for data retention we have configurable retention policies and exports; for Private you control full disk encryption keys.
[02:42] Mateo: what about latency trade-offs? hosted sounds easy but cost is unknown; dedicated feels like guaranteed latency but heavy commit.
[02:52] Maya: exactly. hosted is best for quick onramp — you can run small pilots with credits. dedicated (reserved GPU pool) reduces per-token cost at scale and gives capacity guarantees. private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulatory needs or strict data residency. there's also a middle path — dedicated in a customer VPC.
[03:12] Lena: do you have examples of typical p95 latency numbers on hosted for small models? we want realistic baselines.
[03:20] Elliot: we publish benchmark profiles and we can run a mini-benchmark using a snippet of your workload. hosted p95 for classification on mid-sized open models is often ~70-120ms depending on seq len; there's variability. we'll share the spreadsheet.
[03:38] Priya: are those numbers for streaming or synchronous?
[03:42] Maya: synchronous single-request numbers; streaming adds overhead but is similar for short responses. caching of prefixes and KV cache helps if you're rerunning repeats.
[03:51] Mateo: you said KV cache — we read a doc where it's spelled K V cash — sometimes transcripts have oddities — ha.
[03:58] Jordan: yeah fireflies likes K V cash sometimes.
[04:03] (laughter)
[04:10] Lena: what's the time to spin a dedicated pool? if the pilot goes well and we want predictable latency, how fast can dedicated be provisioned?
[04:18] Maya: provisioning dedicated takes ~1-2 weeks depending on region and capacity, but for an eval you can do hosted then transition with canary rollout. we support autoscaling policies and burst capacity for peaks.
[04:33] Samir: and compliance — SOC2? ISO? audit logs retention?
[04:36] Jordan: we are SOC 2 compliant, and provide audit logs; we'll attach SOC2 report and our security-pack doc after the call.
[04:45] Mateo: good. cost model — do you have sample pricing for a pilot of ~100k tokens/month?
[04:52] Jordan: we'll send a tailored example. quick note: hosted is usage-based. dedicated is commit-based with lower per-token. we'll include a 3-month cost projection for both paths.
[05:07] Priya: how do we evaluate model quality regressions since our routing depends on tight thresholds?
[05:12] Maya: Redwood Optimize ties prompt sets to quality monitoring — you can run evals automatically and get regression alerts tied to your test prompts. we recommend a small eval suite during pilot.
[05:25] Lena: timeline — we aim to decide pilot approach in 2 weeks and start a pilot in 3–4 weeks. is that feasible?
[05:32] Maya: absolutely. plan: hosted pilot with free credits and console access this week, run mini-bench and eval, then reconvene for SE deep dive to plan dedicated/private if needed.
[05:45] Jordan: i'll provision credits after the call and invite your team to the console.
[05:50] Mateo: great. on the technical side, can we run a benchmark that simulates our 120ms p95 requirement? we'd like instructions so our SRE can run it locally too.
[06:00] Elliot: yes — we'll provide a benchmark script and a small harness. small caveat: network egress and geographic distance affect p95; we recommend running tests from your region.
[06:12] Samir: what about VPC/private options — if we need EU-only residency, can that be done without on-prem?
[06:19] Maya: yes, Private in an EU VPC or Dedicated in eu-region with data residency controls. for strict regulatory needs we can discuss on-prem appliance.
[06:28] Lena: any notable gotchas? we've seen vendors with opaque throttling or burst limits that cause flakey SLAs during spikes.
[06:36] Jordan: we expose rate limits, quotas, and have burst capacity options; console shows token-level latency and cost breakdowns so you can detect cost spikes. plus automatic fallback policies to keep routing live in a degraded mode.
[06:55] Priya: curious about SDKs — we primarily use Go and Python.
[06:58] Maya: we have python and node first-class SDKs; Go is community SDK but we provide examples and support.
[07:06] Mateo: any notes on quantization or reduced-precision models? cost's a worry.
[07:11] Elliot: we support quantized model variants and can recommend quantization profiles for your workload using Optimize. often you get 2–3x cost reductions with small latency tradeoff, but for p95-sensitive paths we test.
[07:25] Lena: let's talk stakeholders — who else needs to be looped in? procurement for contract terms, security for SOC2 review, SRE for benchmarking.
[07:33] Jordan: noted. we'll include procurement-friendly language in the follow-up and cc security docs.
[07:38] (brief pause)
[07:45] Jordan: quick demo offer — we can do a 45–60 minute SE deep dive next week to run a live mini-benchmark and walk through the console. does next Tues or Wed work?
[07:55] Priya: Wed morning our time works.
[07:58] Jordan: booked.
[08:02] Lena: thanks — last question: are there common mistakes customers make during pilot?
[08:07] Maya: yep — mixing production traffic into pilot, not pinning model versions, and not setting up rollout/fallback policies. we can share a pilot checklist.
[08:18] Mateo: good to see that.
[08:20] Jordan: ok we'll recap: jordan send pricing and credits, maya send bench script and security pack, mateo send residency regions. schedule se deep dive wed. anything else?
[08:32] Samir: no, that's it
[08:34] Lena: thanks everyone
[08:36] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up by EOD with links and next steps.
